findings.title: Interruption and resume behaviour required by SKILL-006 is instructed nowhere in the runtime package
findings.requirement: SKILL-006 line 46: 'On interruption, preserve the current phase and evidence; resume by checking their identities and the session assignment again.' SKILL-006 line 85: 'If the worktree or active run changes, re-establish the appropriate baseline and evidence before resuming.'

affected.section: absent throughout; the natural home is the Stopping section (lines 233-249)
'Resume and custody' (line 90) - present but does not carry the requirement

evidence: Case-insensitive search for 'interrupt', 'resum' and 're-establish' across SKILL.md and all four files in references/ returns zero hits.

The only package hit is assets/handoff.md line 90 '## Resume and custody', whose six bullets are fields of a completed handoff document (task output readback, this handoff's location, its receipt, worktree disposition, external gate state, invalidating conditions). A session interrupted mid-phase never reaches the handoff step, so that section is unreachable for this condition.

diff of docs/mvp/templates/shared/handoff.md against assets/handoff.md shows the 'You are here' section lost the row 'Current phase: {{phase}}' - the one field in the shared template that recorded the phase.
The sibling package devforge-evaluate-expert SKILL.md carries an explicit interruption paragraph in its Stopping section, so the omission is not a house-style choice.
findings.demonstrated_impact: A planning session interrupted mid-phase has no instruction to preserve the phase reached, the frozen input identities or the outputs already written, and no instruction to re-read the session assignment and re-check the recorded digests before it resumes writing. That re-check is the precondition the package's own staleness rule (references/upstream-resolution.md) and ownership-collision rule (references/readiness-check.md) both depend on, so the omission reopens the two failures the rest of the package handles carefully.
findings.author_record_conflict: spec-mapping.md line 58 maps this requirement to assets/handoff.md 'Resume and custody' and references/upstream-resolution.md 'When a cited revision no longer matches'. Neither carries it; the second addresses a moved revision during normal operation, not resumption after an interruption.
findings.smallest_repair: Add one short paragraph to SKILL.md's Stopping section (or a subsection of references/readiness-check.md linked from phase 4): on interruption, preserve the phase reached, the frozen input identities and any outputs already written; on resume, re-read the session assignment and re-check the recorded digests before writing further, and treat a changed input as a new iteration rather than a continuation. Optionally restore the 'Current phase' row to assets/handoff.md's 'You are here' section, which also closes F-007.
findings.preserve: Every other stopping and error behaviour, the finite completion condition, and the instruction not to add another pass of polish.
findings.rerun: A new tier-B case staging an interrupted session is needed; none exists.

findings.title: The out-of-scope routing required by the specification's acceptance table exists only in the frontmatter description, not in the body
findings.requirement: SKILL-006 line 69, Validation and behavioral acceptance: 'Out of scope | Ask to brainstorm alternatives without selected scope | Routes to brainstorm or define-product.'
evidence: grep -n 'brainstorm|define-product' over SKILL.md matches line 3, the frontmatter description, and nothing else. Zero matches anywhere in references/ or assets/.

The operative body instruction for a missing required input is 'name it, name the work it blocks, continue with the part of the partition that does not depend on it', which names no receiving sibling.
The candidate's own evals.json id 4 and cases.jsonl PL-B-005 grade exactly the naming of a sibling.
findings.demonstrated_impact: The required observation for this acceptance case is that the response names a receiving sibling. Once the body is loaded it is the operative guidance, and it contains no such instruction; the missing-input rule pulls toward continuing to partition a request that should not be partitioned at all. Mitigating: the description carries the exclusion unambiguously and Claude keeps a description in context, so the routing basis is not wholly absent - which is why this is MINOR rather than MAJOR.
findings.author_record_conflict: spec-mapping.md line 78 claims coverage at 'SKILL.md description exclusions; section Stopping'. The Stopping section contains neither sibling name.
findings.smallest_repair: Add one sentence to SKILL.md's 'Required inputs' missing-input paragraph or to Stopping: when no scope has been adopted at all, do not partition - name early-stage exploration as the work and route it to devforge-brainstorm, or to devforge-define-product where the open question is what the scope should contain, keeping what is suggested separate from what is installed.
findings.preserve: The three near-miss exclusions in the description exactly as they are, and the existing missing-input behaviour for the case where scope exists but one input is absent.
findings.rerun: evals.json id 4 and PL-B-005 after the change.

findings.title: PL-PKG-001 gates four mode-independent structural assertions behind case-level mode 'installed', making them unobtainable without an installed copy
findings.requirement: The case file's own purpose: to supply deterministic structural observations for this package. Skill-authoring contract, separately reported tiers.
evidence: runner-out/pkg-source.jsonl: PL-PKG-001 A1 through A5 are all INDETERMINATE with reason "the case declares mode 'installed' and this run used 'source'".
The frozen run_cases.py applies the case-level mode to every assertion in the case, not only to the assertions that depend on installation.

runner-out/evaluator-added-source.jsonl: EV-PKG-001 A1-A4, the identical four assertions with no mode declaration, all return MATCH (frontmatter present; name and description populated; name == folder; 7 local links all resolve).
Only A5 (path_absent evals) is genuinely mode-dependent: evals/ must be present in a source tree.
findings.demonstrated_impact: The package's only deterministic frontmatter, name/folder and SKILL.md link-resolution observations cannot be obtained in any assignment that has no installed copy - which is every assignment so far, including this one. The evaluator had to author a replacement case to observe them.
findings.smallest_repair: Split PL-PKG-001: keep A1-A4 in a case with no 'mode' key, and move A5 into its own case carrying "mode": "installed" with a title saying it is only observable against an installed copy.
findings.preserve: The assertions themselves, their args and PL-PKG-002 unchanged.
findings.rerun: The split cases in both source and installed mode.

evidence: The record pins scripts/run_cases.py sha256 d1fb18689eeea31f8facde4e3de1507320e74ffb349f547f9db2201395bb132d and scripts/graders.py sha256 7c03e7b2137787035c995787b232a7bf8d801c88672675bacf4359a8cdb38c13 at commit e52ac596cbf790dfa156d883852d392c512fdbcc, and calls the dependency 'PENDING AND UNMERGED'.
The frozen validator at e641797 carries run_cases.py 95ca2abf77a5baf249694ad37d67a74949b567acd5164fd309724cbc576583e2 and graders.py 1b7a27a37e1fb8b2e36b1822bc23227c69e6300243e1b49b8caa848e3feca69f.

git diff e52ac59..e641797 over those paths: graders.py +108 lines, run_cases.py +55 lines, runner-interface.md +32 lines, including new whole-file rejection of unknown case-level and assertion-level keys.

Recheck performed by this evaluation: the ten-entry GRADERS registry is byte-identical across the two revisions; every case key used (assertions, candidate_subpath, case_id, expectations, files, mode, prompt, tier, title) and every assertion key used (args, assertion_id, expect, grader, routed_to) is inside the frozen runner's permitted sets; the file loaded and produced 17 case records at exit 0 in all three candidate runs.

findings.title: recording-rules.md narrows producer.skill_revision beyond the contract it says it only restates, and offers 'unknown' without routing it to missing_inputs
findings.requirement: docs/mvp/artifact-contract.md, Standard envelope: 'producer | Native skill name and exact installed skill revision/digest'.
evidence: The reference states: 'producer.skill_revision is the SHA-256 of the installed SKILL.md file's bytes - one file. It is not a digest of the package and not the plugin version... Where nothing observable gives you the value, unknown is the honest entry.'

grep skill_revision docs/mvp/artifact-contract.md returns no hits; the contract defines the field only as 'exact installed skill revision/digest' and supplies no unknown fallback for producer (it supplies one for execution_ref: null plus missing_inputs).
The reference opens by claiming 'It restates; it does not extend or waive that contract, and where the two differ the contract governs.'
evals/fixtures/good/EPIC-001.md carries skill_revision: 'unknown (synthetic fixture; no installed skill produced these bytes)'.
findings.demonstrated_impact: An epic or story could carry producer.skill_revision: unknown with an empty missing_inputs and still be presented as a complete result, while the contract requires the exact installed revision or digest. The narrowing itself is useful and honest, and the reference does declare the contract to govern, which is why this is ADVISORY rather than a FAIL.
findings.smallest_repair: Add to that paragraph that an unknown producer revision is a missing required fact and belongs in missing_inputs, and mark the one-file definition explicitly as this package's narrowing rather than a contract restatement.
findings.preserve: The distinction between a SKILL.md digest, a package digest and a plugin version, which is the useful part.
findings.rerun: None; a new artifact assertion on producer.skill_revision could be added.
